prompt: Stage 2-6, level 4, 14 gold, 4 XP from level 5, 84 HP after three losses in a row. A 2-star bruiser is on your bench and your four board units all survive to the end of fights, barely losing. Buying XP costs 4 gold for 4 XP. Do you buy?

options.label: Buy 4 XP: the 2-star bruiser becomes your fifth unit and turns close losses into wins
Hold the 14 gold so you reach 20 next round and earn 2 interest
Refresh the shop twice (4 gold) looking for something better than the bruiser

explanation:
Buy XP when one more unit would win the fights you are currently losing, and that is exactly this board. Your fights are close and you have a ready 2-star that cannot fit. One purchase adds it: 14 gold becomes 10, still 1 interest. Holding for 20 gold gains 1 gold of interest next round and costs you the fight in front of you; at three losses in a row with 84 HP the HP is the real price, and the stage-3 fights that follow hit harder.

Refreshing is the worst of the three: it spends the same 4 gold on a chance of a unit that still would not fit at level 4. The level is the bottleneck, not the shop. Level 5 at 2-5 or 2-6 is also the standard timing, so you are not paying for anything unusual.
principle: When a fifth unit wins the next fight, 4 gold of XP is the best buy on the screen.
commonMistake: Chasing an interest breakpoint while a ready 2-star sits on the bench and the board keeps losing.
hint: Ask what stops the bruiser from fighting right now, and whether 1 extra interest gold is worth another loss at 2-6.
